# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1089

## Korean source

```text
  1|1089화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|
  6|유시(酉時)에 막 접어들 무렵, 어느덧 서산으로 조금씩 기울어 가는 태양을 본 늙은 거지는 혼잣말처럼 중얼거렸다.
  7|
  8|“희한하군. 아직 해가 질 시간이 아닌데.”
  9|
 10|그 말에 가까운 모닥불 근처에 옹기종기 모여있던 또 다른 거지들이 반응했다.
 11|
 12|“그럼 지금 같은 계절에 이런 날씨인 건 말이 되고요?”
 13|
 14|“맞지. 하루 이틀 일도 아니고.”
 15|
 16|“분타주(分舵主)님도 괜히 거기서 찬바람 맞지 마시고, 와서 모닥불이나 좀 쬐시우. 뜨뜻한 국물도 한 사발 하시고.”
 17|
 18|하긴, 틀린 말은 아니다.
 19|
 20|세상이 요지경이 된 것은 어제오늘 일이 아니었으니까.
 21|
 22|늙은 거지, 아니 개방의 청해성 서녕 분타주인 만총은 작게 한숨을 내쉬며 모닥불로 걸음을 옮겼다.
 23|
 24|후개(後丐)인 궁기방은 이미 서녕으로 돌아간 지 여러 날이었지만, 휘하의 개방도 삼십여 명과 함께 남아 정보를 수집하고 있던 그였다.
 25|
 26|“먹을 것 좀 있나?”
 27|
 28|“그 무슨 당연한 말씀을. 가진 거라고는 쥐뿔도 없어도 어떻게든 배는 채우는 게 우리 아니오?”
 29|
 30|“정찰 나가 있는 놈들 몫은 남겨뒀고?”
 31|
 32|“어허. 누굴 상도덕도 모르는 거지로 보시나. 걱정 마시우. 그놈들도 돌아와서 배터지게 먹을 만큼 해뒀수.”
 33|
 34|누런 이를 드러내며 씩 웃은 거지 하나가 김이 모락모락 피어오르는 사발을 내밀자, 만총이 자신도 모르게 입맛을 다셨다.
 35|
 36|“향은 끝내주는구먼.”
 37|
 38|“드시기나 하슈. 향만 끝내주는 게 아니라는 걸 알게 될 테니까.”
 39|
 40|과연 그 말은 사실이었다. 
 41|
 42|불과 촌각 만에 게 눈 감추듯 사발을 싹 비운 만총은 부른 배를 두드리며 만족스러운 미소를 지었다.
 43|
 44|비록 겉보기에는 잡탕도 이런 잡탕이 없었지만, 청해호(靑海湖)에서 갓 잡은 물고기로 만든 덕분인지 그 맛은 일류 숙수가 만든 것처럼 훌륭하게 느껴졌다.
 45|
 46|‘하긴, 몸도 늙었는데 이런 호사라도 있어야지.’
 47|
 48|포만감에 나른해진 만총은 생선 가시로 이를 쑤시며 주변을 둘러보았다.
 49|
 50|천천히 노을빛에 젖어 들어가는 청해호의 강물을 보고 있자니, 근심과 걱정도 잠시나마 씻겨 내려가는 듯한 기분이었다.
 51|
 52|물론, 현실은 여전히 암담하기만 했지만.
 53|
 54|‘경치 좋고 배부르면 뭣하나. 그놈들이 없어지기 전까지는 발 뻗고 자지도 못하는 것을.’
 55|
 56|암천. 그 무시무시한 악귀들을 떠올리자 만총의 얼굴에 그림자가 드리워졌다.
 57|
 58|지금으로부터 약 나흘 전, 진태경을 비롯한 지원군들이 이곳을 지나 서녕에 합류한 후에도 상황은 좀처럼 나아지지 않았다.
 59|
 60|아니, 찰나의 희망을 짓밟기라도 하듯 하루가 다르게 악화 되어 가는 중이었다.
 61|
 62|‘이대로면 영락없이 앞뒤로 포위당할 텐데……젠장, 용코로 걸렸군.’
 63|
 64|당장 곤륜산을 점령한 암천의 대군만 생각해도 등골이 서늘해질 정도인데, 후방에서는 중원 무림의 뒤통수를 거하게 후려친 도적놈들이 개미 떼처럼 몰려들고 있다고 했다.
 65|
 66|이런 와중에 그나마 다행인 점이 있다면 딱 하나.
 67|
 68|암천의 본대가 아직 본격적인 움직임을 보이지 않고 있다는 것이었다.
 69|
 70|‘하지만 이제는 그것도 시간 문제. 놈들은 반드시 들이닥친다. 그것도 빠른 시일 내에.’
 71|
 72|생각이 거기까지 미치자 조금 전 느꼈던 포만감이 싹 가시고, 불안과 두려움이 빈자리를 채웠다.
 73|
 74|“……염병할.”
 75|
 76|삽시간에 기분이 더러워진 만총은 손 닿은 곳에 있던 자갈을 주워 냅다 내던졌다.
 77|
 78|쐐애액!
 79|
 80|행색은 남루해도 그 역시 개방에서 제법 잔뼈가 굵은 분타주 급의 고수. 
 81|
 82|손끝을 떠난 자갈이 끝없이 펼쳐진 청해호를 향해 쏘아졌다.
 83|
 84|촤아아악!
 85|
 86|거칠게 갈라지는 수면. 그제야 답답했던 속이 조금이나마 풀린 만총은 콧김을 뿜으며 돌아섰다.
 87|
 88|아니, 돌아서려고 했다.
 89|
 90|자갈로 인해 일어난 파문이 가라앉으며, 서서히 평온함을 되찾는 강물을 보기 전까지는.
 91|
 92|‘뭐지?’
 93|
 94|그리고 그 불현듯 찾아온 기시감의 정체를, 만총은 그리 오래되지 않아 깨달을 수 있었다.
 95|
 96|‘색. 강물의 색이…….’
 97|
 98|어둡다.
 99|
100|아니, 먹물이라도 풀어놓을 것처럼 새카맸다.
101|
102|불과 촌각 전까지만 하더라도 노을빛에 물들어 있던 청해호의 강물은 더 이상 아름답지 않았고, 귓가로 두런두런 들려오는 대화는 유난히도 꺼림칙했다.
103|
104|“아따, 오늘따라 왜 이리 빨리 어두워진대? 그래도 평소에는 노을 지는 데만 한 식경은 걸리더만.”
105|
106|“우리가 따져봤자 뭘 어쩌겠소. 그냥 그런 갑다 해야지. 정찰간 놈들 돌아오기 전에 밥이나 더 드쇼.”
107|
108|“나야 물론 좋지. 아, 분타주께서도 한술 더 뜨시렵니까?”
109|
110|만총은 대답하지 않았다.
111|
112|정확히는 대답할 수 없었다.
113|
114|지금 이 순간, 그의 본능이 머릿속에 붉은 경종을 울리고 있었으니까.
115|
116|‘이건……뭔가 이상하다.’
117|
118|물론 다른 개방도들의 반응처럼 별 것 아닌 일일 수도 있다.
119|
120|추수철이 오기도 전에 서리가 내리고, 인간 같지도 않은 외관을 지닌 거대한 괴물들이 날뛰는 마당에 뭘 더 놀랄 것이 있겠나.
121|
122|그러나 알 수 없는 직감이 있었다.
123|
124|환갑이 넘은 나이까지 쌓아온 경륜, 노강호로서 뼈에 새겨진 듯한 본능이.
125|
126|“정찰대, 정찰대는 언제쯤 돌아온다더냐?”
127|
128|“예? 아니 갑자기 그건 왜.”
129|
130|“대답하거라, 어서!”
131|
132|늘 사람 좋던 늙은 분타주의 불호령에, 당황한 개방도들이 더듬더듬 입을 열었다.
133|
134|“고, 곧 올 겁니다요.”
135|
136|“그, 사실 평소보다 반 각 정도 늦긴 했습니다만 코앞까진 왔을 테니 분타주께서 걱정하실 필요는……어라?”
137|
138|대답하던 개방도 중 하나가 눈을 동그랗게 뜨며 만총의 어깨너머를 바라보자, 모두의 시선이 그곳을 향해 쏠렸다.
139|
140|약 이백여 장 밖에 자리 잡은 야트막한 언덕.
141|
142|그 위로 자그마한 점처럼 막 모습을 드러낸 한 무리의 인마(人馬)가 흐릿한 어둠을 뚫고 천천히 언덕을 내려오고 있었다.
143|
144|“호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다더니. 마침 때맞춰 왔구먼.”
145|
146|“저저, 게을러터진 놈들 같으니라고. 늦은 주제에 설렁설렁 오면 쓰나?”
147|
148|“분타주께서는 이만 고정하시우. 내 아주 이번 기회에 혼쭐을 낼 터이니.”
149|
150|모두가 만총의 눈치를 살피며 한 마디씩을 던지던 그때, 침잠한 눈빛으로 정찰대를 응시하던 그가 신음처럼 뇌까렸다.
151|
152|“열둘.”
153|
154|“예?”
155|
156|“열둘이다. 내 눈이 잘못된 것이 아니라면.”
157|
158|“그게 무…….”
159|
160|뜬금없는 말에 의문을 표하던 누군가가 문득 말꼬리를 흐렸다.
161|
162|지금으로부터 약 두 시진 전, 인근을 둘러보기 위해 떠났던 정찰대의 머릿수는 총 열 명이었으니까.
163|
164|“그, 그렇다는 건.”
165|
166|“둘 중 하나겠지. 천운으로 살아남은 생존자를 구했거나.”
167|
168|손때 묻은 철곤(鐵棍)을 허릿춤에서 빼어 들며, 만총이 나직이 덧붙였다.
169|
170|“산 채로 씹어 먹어도 시원치 않을 어떤 개자식들이, 정찰대 행세를 하고 있거나.”
171|
172|“……!”
173|
174|“지금 당장 배로 이동한다. 우선 닻을 올리고 거리를 벌린 후에 상황을 지켜볼 것이다.”
175|
176|“며, 명을 받듭니다!”
177|
178|그제야 상황의 심각성을 알아차린 이들은 언제 그랬냐는 듯 일사불란하게 움직였다. 
179|
180|그리고 강가에 정박시켜두었던 배에 올라타 빠르게 노를 저은 개방도들이 충분한 거리를 벌렸을 때쯤에는, 적인지 아군인지 모를 정체불명의 무리가 그들이 피워두었던 모닥불 근처까지 다다라 있었다.
181|
182|“석삼이, 석삼이 거기 있는가!”
183|
184|불쑥 울려 퍼진 만총의 외침에, 어느덧 확연히 짙어진 어둠 너머에서 대답이 들려왔다.
185|
186|“나 여기 있네! 무슨 일인가?”
187|
188|그 순간, 만총의 얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳었다.
189|
190|아니, 그를 포함한 모든 개방도가 마찬가지였다.
191|
192|청해호에 머무르던 이들 중, 분타주이자 최연장자인 만총에게 하대를 할 수 있는 개방도는 한 명도 없었으니까.
193|
194|하지만 다른 무엇보다 가장 큰 충격을 받은 부분은, 짙은 어둠 너머에서 들려온 목소리가 그들이 아는 석삼이의 것과 똑같다는 것이었다.
195|
196|“부, 분타주.”
197|
198|귀신이라도 목격한 것처럼 창백한 얼굴을 한 개방도들을 뒤로한 채, 이를 악문 만총이 다시금 외쳤다.
199|
200|“네놈들은 누구냐!”
201|
202|잠시 정적이 흘렀다. 
203|
204|찰나에 불과했으나 그 어느 때보다 길고, 영원처럼 느껴지는 정적이.
205|
206|그리고 질식할 것만 같은 그 적막함을 단숨에 깨트리는, 낯선 목소리가 불현듯 울려 퍼졌다. 
207|
208|“이런. 거지새끼들이라 그런지 눈치가 빠르군.”
209|
210|웃음기마저 묻어있는 들뜬 음성과 함께, 아직 꺼지지 않은 모닥불을 향해 윤곽으로만 보이던 형체가 모습을 드러냈다.
211|
212|타다닥.
213|
214|허공으로 피어오르는 불똥 사이, 일말의 소음도 없이 자갈밭을 가로지른 한 쌍의 인마를 목격한 만총이 눈을 부릅떴다.
215|
216|“이, 이게 무슨……!”
217|
218|그는 일순간 할 말을 잃었다.
219|
220|새하얀 뼈를 훤히 드러낸 해골마의 모습 때문이기도 했지만, 그 위에 태연히 앉아있는 사내에게서 지금껏 경험해 본 적 없는 공포를 느꼈기 때문이었다.
221|
222|히죽.
223|
224|이질적으로까지 보이는 새하얀 이빨이, 맹수의 그것처럼 날카로운 송곳니가 드러난다.
225|
226|그뿐인가.
227|
228|먼 거리에서도 선명하게 번뜩이는 핏빛 눈동자는, 마주한 것만으로도 심신을 옭매는 듯했다.
229|
230|“네, 네놈은.”
231|
232|파르르 신형을 떠는 만총을 향해, 사내가 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.
233|
234|“뭐, 대충 알잖아. 누구인지.”
235|
236|더욱더 큰 공포를 불러일으키는 천연덕스러운 태도. 
237|
238|그러나 만총은 가까스로 목소리를 쥐어 짜냈다.
239|
240|“정찰대는……그들은 어찌 되었느냐.”
241|
242|“크. 감동적인데. 구걸하면서 쌓은 정이 상당한가 봐?”
243|
244|“놈! 묻는 말에 대답하지 못할까!”
245|
246|“이거 거지 무서워서 말이야 제대로 하겠나. 알겠어, 알겠으니까 너무 흥분하지 말라고.”
247|
248|진정하라는 듯 손을 내저은 사내가 입맛을 다셨다.
249|
250|“결론만 말하자면, 다들 좋은 곳으로 갔지. 별로 맛은 없었지만.”
251|
252|“뭐, 뭐라?”
253|
254|감히 입에 담을 수조차 없는 어떠한 짐작으로 굳어버린 만총의 모습에, 사내가 눈살을 찌푸렸다. 
255|
256|“아, 불쾌한 오해는 하지 마. 비루먹은 거지새끼들이라 그런지 몸뚱어리도 영 아니더라고. 장난도 칠 겸 피만 조금 빨아먹은 게 전부니까.”
257|
258|“……!”
259|
260|“왜, 당신이 생각하기에는 영 별로였나? 그래도 목소리는 제법 감쪽같았을 텐데.”
261|
262|으득.
263|

“W-well, they’re about half a gak later than usual, but they must be close by now. There’s no need to worry, Branch Master… Huh?”

[P64]
One of the disciples trailed off, eyes widening as he looked over Man Chong’s shoulder. Everyone turned.

[P65]
On a low hill about two hundred zhang away, a group of men and horses had just appeared, tiny as specks. They were slowly descending through the gathering darkness.

[P66]
“Speak of the devil. There they are.”

[P67]
“Look at those lazy bastards. They’re already late, and now they’re taking their sweet time?”

[P68]
“Branch Master, you can settle down. I’ll give them a proper scolding.”

[P69]
As the others offered excuses while watching his expression, Man Chong stared at the patrol and murmured, almost like a groan.

[P70]
“Twelve.”

[P71]
“What?”

[P72]
“Twelve. Unless my eyes are playing tricks on me.”

[P73]
“What does that—”

[P74]
The disciple’s question died on his lips.

[P75]
The patrol that had left to survey the area about two shichen ago had numbered ten.

[P76]
“Th-that means…”

[P77]
“One of two things. Either they found survivors who escaped by sheer luck…”

[P78]
Man Chong drew the iron staff, worn smooth from years of handling, from his waist and added quietly,

[P79]
“Or some sons of bitches who deserve to be chewed up alive are pretending to be the patrol.”

[P80]
“…!”

[P81]
“Get to the boat. Raise anchor, put some distance between us, and then we’ll see what they do.”

[P82]
“Y-yes, Branch Master!”

[P83]
At last grasping the danger, the disciples moved as one.

[P84]
By the time they’d boarded the boat moored by the shore and rowed a safe distance away, the unidentified group had reached the campfire they’d left behind.

[P85]
“Seok Sam! Seok Sam, are you there?”

[P86]
An answer came from beyond the darkness, which had grown noticeably deeper.

[P87]
“I’m here! What is it?”

[P88]
Man Chong’s face went rigid.

[P89]
So did every other Beggars’ Sect disciple’s. Not one of those staying at Qinghai Lake would have addressed Man Chong—their Branch Master and the oldest among them—as an equal.

[P90]
Worse, the voice from the darkness sounded exactly like Seok Sam’s.

[P91]
“B-Branch Master…”

[P92]
Leaving the pale-faced disciples behind him, Man Chong gritted his teeth and shouted again.

[P93]
“Who are you bastards?”

[P94]
Silence followed. It lasted only a moment, yet felt longer than any silence he’d ever known.

[P95]
Then an unfamiliar voice shattered it.

[P96]
“Well, I guess beggar bastards are quick on the uptake.”

[P97]
There was even a hint of laughter in the man’s buoyant voice. A shape that had been nothing but a silhouette emerged into the light of the still-burning campfire.

[P98]
*Tap-tap.*

[P99]
Amid the sparks rising into the air, a man and horse crossed the gravel without the slightest sound. Man Chong’s eyes widened.

[P100]
“W-what is that…?”

[P101]
For a moment, he couldn’t speak.

[P102]
The horse was a skeleton, its white bones exposed. But it was the man seated so casually on its back who filled him with a fear unlike anything he’d ever known.

[P103]
The man grinned, baring unnaturally white teeth and fangs as sharp as a wild beast’s.

[P104]
His blood-red eyes gleamed even at this distance. Just meeting his gaze felt as though it bound Man Chong’s body and mind.

[P105]
“Y-you…”

[P106]
The man shrugged at the trembling Man Chong.

[P107]
“You know who I am, more or less.”

[P108]
His nonchalance only made him more terrifying. Man Chong forced out a question.

[P109]
“The patrol… What happened to them?”

[P110]
“Aw. How touching. All that begging together must have made you close.”

[P111]
“You bastard! Answer me!”

[P112]
“How am I supposed to talk with a beggar yelling at me? Fine, fine. Don’t get so worked up.”

[P113]
The man waved a hand as though calming him down, then smacked his lips.

[P114]
“To sum it up, they’ve gone to a better place. Didn’t taste like much, though.”

[P115]
“W-what did you say?”

[P116]
Man Chong froze at a thought too horrible to put into words. The man frowned.

[P117]
“Hey, don’t get the wrong idea. They were mangy beggar bastards, and their bodies weren’t much good either. I only drank a little blood to have some fun.”

[P118]
“…!”

[P119]
“What? Was that not good enough for you? I thought I got the voice pretty close.”

[P120]
*Grit.*

[P121]
The taste of blood filled Man Chong’s mouth. Still, he clenched his teeth harder.

[P122]
It wasn’t only rage at losing a subordinate who had been like a brother to him. He had to do this—had to hold on somehow—to bear the fear tightening its grip on him with every passing moment.

[P123]
Dark arts.

[P124]
Never had those words felt so chilling. Never had someone a hundred zhang away made him feel as though his head might come off at any moment.

[P125]
“So you’re the one. The leader we’ve heard about.”

[P126]
“Well, let’s say I am. At least here, that person has entrusted everything to me.”

[P127]
The man—the Blood Lord—smiled at Man Chong.

[P128]
Then he slowly swept his gaze over the twenty Beggars’ Sect disciples, frozen like statues around him, and spoke.

[P129]
“So, who’ll it be?”

[P130]
“What?”

[P131]
“I’m planning to let at least one of you live. One of you gets to survive, and I get someone to deliver a message. Good for both sides, isn’t it?”

[P132]
“…!”

[P133]
“Look at your faces. What, did you think you could just run away?”

[P134]
The Blood Lord grinned at their rigid faces a hundred zhang away, then turned to look behind him.

[P135]
“Time to get moving, don’t you think? You have to do it anyway.”

[P136]
At his words, one of the figures waiting in the darkness stepped forward.

[P137]
*Swish.*

[P138]
Long robes brushed the gravel. As if the Blood Lord weren’t worth answering, the Grand Mage passed him, reached the lakeshore, and extended her hand.

[P139]
“Cold north wind…”

[P140]
*Wooooom.*

[P141]
The air trembled. A vast chill swept across Qinghai Lake.

[P142]
And then Man Chong saw it.

[P143]
“Freeze.”

[P144]
*Crack-crack-crack!*

[P145]
Ice spread across Qinghai Lake, turning it white.

[P146]
“…!”

[P147]
“…!”

[P148]
Man Chong and all twenty Beggars’ Sect disciples stared, wide-eyed.

[P149]
A miracle that should not—and could not—exist.

[P150]
Faced with that impossible sight, they could do nothing.

[P151]
Not when the foul stench of monsters began to drift toward them from beyond the thick darkness.

[P152]
Not when the Blood Lord crossed the frozen lake as casually as if out for a stroll, climbed onto the bow of their boat, and looked down at them.

[P153]
“Whoever survives, go tell them. I—the Blood Lord—am coming.”

[P154]
Man Chong forced out his voice with all the strength he had left.

[P155]
“You’ll never win—”

[P156]
*Crunch!*

[P157]
Scarlet blood sprayed across the white ice.

[P158]
“So, have you decided who gets to survive?”

[P159]
In the cold, deep night, the Blood Lord’s blood-red eyes gleamed.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

“Seok Sam! Seok Sam, are you there?”

[P86]
An answer came from beyond the darkness, which had grown noticeably deeper.

[P87]
“I’m here! What is it?”

[P88]
Man Chong’s face went rigid.

[P89]
So did every other Beggars’ Sect disciple’s. Not one of those staying at Qinghai Lake would have addressed Man Chong—their Branch Master and the oldest among them—as an equal.

[P90]
Worse, the voice from the darkness sounded exactly like Seok Sam’s.

[P91]
“B-Branch Master…”

[P92]
Leaving the pale-faced disciples behind him, Man Chong gritted his teeth and shouted again.

[P93]
“Who are you bastards?”

[P94]
Silence followed. It lasted only a moment, yet felt longer than any silence he’d ever known.

[P95]
Then an unfamiliar voice shattered it.

[P96]
“Well, I guess beggar bastards are quick on the uptake.”

[P97]
There was even a hint of laughter in the man’s buoyant voice. A shape that had been nothing but a silhouette emerged into the light of the still-burning campfire.

[P98]
*Tap-tap.*

[P99]
Amid the sparks rising into the air, a man and horse crossed the gravel without the slightest sound. Man Chong’s eyes widened.

[P100]
“W-what is that…?”

[P101]
For a moment, he couldn’t speak.

[P102]
The horse was a skeleton, its white bones exposed. But it was the man seated so casually on its back who filled him with a fear unlike anything he’d ever known.

[P103]
The man grinned, baring unnaturally white teeth and fangs as sharp as a wild beast’s.

[P104]
His blood-red eyes gleamed even at this distance. Just meeting his gaze felt as though it bound Man Chong’s body and mind.

[P105]
“Y-you…”

[P106]
The man shrugged at the trembling Man Chong.

[P107]
“You know who I am, more or less.”

[P108]
His nonchalance only made him more terrifying. Man Chong forced out a question.

[P109]
“The patrol… What happened to them?”

[P110]
“Aw. How touching. All that begging together must have made you close.”

[P111]
“You bastard! Answer me!”

[P112]
“How am I supposed to talk with a beggar yelling at me? Fine, fine. Don’t get so worked up.”

[P113]
The man waved a hand as though calming him down, then smacked his lips.

[P114]
“To sum it up, they’ve gone to a better place. Didn’t taste like much, though.”

[P115]
“W-what did you say?”

[P116]
Man Chong froze at a thought too horrible to put into words. The man frowned.

[P117]
“Hey, don’t get the wrong idea. They were mangy beggar bastards, and their bodies weren’t much good either. I only drank a little blood to have some fun.”

[P118]
“…!”

[P119]
“What? Was that not good enough for you? I thought I got the voice pretty close.”

[P120]
*Grit.*

[P121]
The taste of blood filled Man Chong’s mouth. Still, he clenched his teeth harder.

[P122]
It wasn’t only rage at losing a subordinate who had been like a brother to him. He had to do this—had to hold on somehow—to bear the fear tightening its grip on him with every passing moment.

[P123]
Dark arts.

[P124]
Never had those words felt so chilling. Never had someone a hundred zhang away made him feel as though his head might come off at any moment.

[P125]
“So you’re the one. The leader we’ve heard about.”

[P126]
“Well, let’s say I am. At least here, that person has entrusted everything to me.”

[P127]
The man—the Blood Lord—smiled at Man Chong.

[P128]
Then he slowly swept his gaze over the twenty Beggars’ Sect disciples, frozen like statues around him, and spoke.

[P129]
“So, who’ll it be?”

[P130]
“What?”

[P131]
“I’m planning to let at least one of you live. One of you gets to survive, and I get someone to deliver a message. Good for both sides, isn’t it?”

[P132]
“…!”

[P133]
“Look at your faces. What, did you think you could just run away?”

[P134]
The Blood Lord grinned at their rigid faces a hundred zhang away, then turned to look behind him.

[P135]
“Time to get moving, don’t you think? You have to do it anyway.”

[P136]
At his words, one of the figures waiting in the darkness stepped forward.

[P137]
*Swish.*

[P138]
Long robes brushed the gravel. As if the Blood Lord weren’t worth answering, the Grand Mage passed him, reached the lakeshore, and extended her hand.

[P139]
“Cold north wind…”

[P140]
*Wooooom.*

[P141]
The air trembled. A vast chill swept across Qinghai Lake.

[P142]
And then Man Chong saw it.

[P143]
“Freeze.”

[P144]
*Crack-crack-crack!*

[P145]
Ice spread across Qinghai Lake, turning it white.

[P146]
“…!”

[P147]
“…!”

[P148]
Man Chong and all twenty Beggars’ Sect disciples stared, wide-eyed.

[P149]
A miracle that should not—and could not—exist.

[P150]
Faced with that impossible sight, they could do nothing.

[P151]
Not when the foul stench of monsters began to drift toward them from beyond the thick darkness.

[P152]
Not when the Blood Lord crossed the frozen lake as casually as if out for a stroll, climbed onto the bow of their boat, and looked down at them.

[P153]
“Whoever survives, go tell them. I—the Blood Lord—am coming.”

[P154]
Man Chong forced out his voice with all the strength he had left.

[P155]
“You’ll never win—”

[P156]
*Crunch!*

[P157]
Scarlet blood sprayed across the white ice.

[P158]
“So, have you decided who gets to survive?”

[P159]
In the cold, deep night, the Blood Lord’s blood-red eyes gleamed.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.
